newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta recovers slightly, but no intervention seen.
newsitem.headline: Peseta recovers slightly, but no intervention seen.

text.p: The Spanish peseta bounced back a bit against the mark after hitting 84.80 on Monday, but dealers ruled out intervention from the Bank of Spain.
They added that the central bank would only enter the market if the peseta broke 85.00 per mark.
"So far we haven't seen the Bank of Spain. When the peseta hit 84.80 per mark the market corrected," a forex dealer said.
By 1140 GMT the peseta was trading at 84.70/73 per mark after touching 84.77/4.80, and ocmpared with early levels of 84.62/65.
The central bank is believed to be keen to hold the peseta in a band between 84.00 and 85.00 per mark in the run-up to EMU and has intervened in recent months to maintain these levels.
The peseta weakened against the mark on Monday as remarks from France over Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) revived fears that Europe's single currency could be delayed.

France's new Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said more time was needed to discuss the so-called stability pact on fiscal discipline after EMU is launched. He added that France needs more time to discuss the economic pillars of the union.
France also reiterated that it was determined to maintain the EMU schedule.
